key_insight: LLMs are not separate from world models; they can be viewed as a special case where the state is token sequences and the only action is predicting the next token, with a continuous path from next-token prediction toward latent-state world modeling.
engineering_relevance: This reframing highlights a practical research roadmap for AI systems: relax token-prediction constraints step by step while preserving scalability, data efficiency, and transformer-based training infrastructure where possible.
method: Defines LLMs as a degenerate world model over token-sequence state space.
Places next-token prediction, multi-token prediction, future-summary prediction, and next-latent prediction on a spectrum toward JEPA-style latent modeling.
Evaluates the tradeoff between richer state representations and the loss of internet-scale self-supervised text data plus token-native transformer simplicity.
evidence_signal: The abstract is a conceptual synthesis rather than an empirical benchmark paper, using the data question (text vs instrumented action environments) and architecture question (transformers vs new primitives for continuous-state prediction) as the main evidence axes.
watch_item: A key implementation risk is that moving beyond tokens may sacrifice the scaling advantages of self-supervised text and require expensive, less standardized action-labeled or embodied data.
paper_title: From Tokens to States: LLMs as a Special Case of World Models and the Continuous Path Beyond
